newsitem.title: GERMANY: BASF, Lynx set up genetic engineering joint-venture.
newsitem.headline: BASF, Lynx set up genetic engineering joint-venture.

text.p: German chemical group BASF AG said Wednesday it will form a biotechnology and genetic engineering joint-venture with California-based Lynx Therapeutics.

BASF plans to invest over 100 million marks ($66 million) in the joint-venture, which will be based in Heidelberg, Germany, and will employ around 60 people, BASF management board member Hans-Juergen Quadbeck-Seeger told journalists in Ludwigshafen.

The main activity of the joint-venture, called BASF-Lynx Bioscience AG, will be working with a process developed by Lynx called MPSS, used to analyse genes when researching materials to develop new pesticides and drugs.

Lynx said that with MPSS it is possible to examine the genetic activity of a cell and the joint-venture parties hope to develop an early-warning system against unwanted side-effects from active substances and chemicals.
BASF will hold a 51 percent stake in the joint venture with the Hayward, Calif.-based Lynx group holding a 49 percent stake, BASF said.
Lynx is the first U.S. company to move to Germany to take part in a joint-venture with a German company in the biotechnology and genetic engineering area.
